Memorable Convention Psi U Service Day: Convention endorsed chapter-wide
day of community outreach
I was privileged to attend the 154th Psi
Upsilon Convention and 1997 Leadership Institute in August. I am writing this
letter to express just how importantand how much fun- this experience is
for all Psi U brothers.
It was an honor to meet so many
brothers from other chapters and to
share perspectives on chapter operations and Psi U in general. More importantly, the chance to be a part of the
legislative process of the Fraternity- and
to have a say- was something I will
never forget. Not every fraternity gives
its undergraduates so much of a say in its
affairs. I was proud to uphold a long
tradition and to do my part.
The Leadership Institute was also a
valuable experience. I know that every
member of the Epsilon Iota delegation
learned important lessons on everything
from chapter leadership to service, and
we have tried to implement them
wherever possible.
My only disapointment was that there
were several chapters which did not
attend. It saddened me that those
chapters not in attendance felt they
needed to let others make the decisions.
Psi U belongs to all of us, regardless of
chapter size, finances, history, etc. I
would implore each chapter to send
delegates and make Convention a
priority. Whether it's your first time, like
it was for me, or if you're a seasoned
veteran, it's a valuable learning experience that you will never forget.

In the early 1800s, literary societies played an important role in the life of college students.
Our Founders, having secured membership in these societies at Union College, valued
opportunities for social interaction which could not be found in the classroom. These
opportunities included reading and writing poetry, discussing literature, and presenting
debates and orations.
Today, with more than 24,000 living alumni, our members have been enriched by the
education and fraternity experience received while attending the leading universities and
colleges in the United States and Canada. So, it should be no surprise that Psi Upsilon has
maintained its literary tradition.
Many of our brothers write-and publish- literary works on a wide range of subjects.
This issue of The DIAMOND of Psi Upsilon highlights several books published by alumni
during the past 12 months. Books published about Psi Us in the past several years are also
featured. The DIAMOND welcomes news of any other new or recent alumni books for

THISISTHE FIRST VOLUMEOF A PROJECTEDFOURvolume edition of the select correspondence, speeches,
and documents of Senator Robert A. Taft, son of President
and Chief Justice William Howard Taft, Beta 1878.
Taft was the most prominent critic of mid-twentiethcentury American liberalism. As a leading Republican
senator and contender for the presidency, he played a
significant role in the development of party politics,
opposing the expanding administrative capacities of the
federal government and the enlargement of America's
international commitments. Selected for inclusion in
Volume 1 are political speeches and other historically
significant documents dealing with subjects of particular
interest to Taft, such as taxation, federal housing, aid to
education, and global military commitments. Recent
events, domestic and foreign, have given contemporary
relevance to his critique.

The study, led by

According to the study,

single-minded, and selfishly
persuasive.

least narcissistic? Calvin Coolidge.
